items.body: ST. PAUL, Minn. — The Minnesota Wild have had few opportunities this season to give their fans a glimpse of what has been one of the most completed and connected teams in the NHL, with an imbalanced early schedule that has them on the road for 18 of their first 26 games. The cameo they made at Grand Casino Arena on Tuesday night was quite a show for the home crowd. With their third consecutive five-plus goal performance, the Wild beat Nashville 7-3 for their 12th straight game without a regulation loss. By going 10-0-2 since Oct. 24, the Wild have the longest point streak in the league this season. Matt Boldy scored twice against the Predators to give the Wild a 5-0 lead with less than a minute elapsed in the second period. They've scored first in all 12 games during the streak that's the third-longest in franchise history. All four lines contributed at least one goal. "That's us. Star defenceman Quinn Hughes, whose reluctance to sign a contract extension, has clearly not created a distraction for him or his teammates. When he's been healthy, the 33-year-old has shown the stellar form that won him the Vezina Trophy with the Boston Bruins. It took him a while, but Ottawa Senators goalie Linus Ullmark is showing the elite form that made him a Vezina Trophy winner. Ullmark had a terrific first season with the Senators in 2024-25, posting a .910 save percentage and a 2.70 goals-against average in 44 appearances. But this season, Ullmark looks back in peak condition in a way he hasn't since first relocating to Canada's capital. The uniforms have retro designs with nods to hockey history and ski culture, a perfect fit for the event and venue. The stadium, the home of University of Utah football, hosted the opening ceremony of the 2002 Winter Olympics and has a mountain backdrop. The first snow of the season here fell overnight, turning the mountains white. “It’s my first time doing this,” said Crouse, who has never played an outdoor game in his 11-year NHL career. “Obviously, the buzz around the state, it’s been pretty amazing. I don’t know if it’s a coincidence, but with the Winter Classic reveal today and the snow, it just feels meant to be.” The Mammoth jersey is Mountain Blue with brown and beige. “UTAH” arches over a throwback Mammoth on the front. items.body: Former goalie will broadcast forward’s next game against Flyers on Thursday The 49-year-old former NHL goalie has spent his entire life in the game, more than half of it in the League as either a player or broadcaster, but never before did he experience what he felt while in the stands at Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg alongside his wife, Melissa, and daughter, Brianna, watching his son, Tyler, score the game-winning goal in his NHL debut with the Ottawa Senators. "I mean, I've had some cool moments in my career; five shutouts in a row stands out," said Boucher, who set the NHL record for longest shutout streak (332:01) in 2003-04. "Win an eight-period game in Pittsburgh in the playoffs, five overtimes (in 2000). But this is better just because it's your kid, and we're all so proud of our children." Tyler Boucher was selected by the Senators with the No. 10 pick in the 2021 NHL Draft, but injuries and four surgeries, two on his knee and one on each shoulder, derailed the 23-year-old's journey to the NHL until he finally got there and scored at 4:04 of the second period to give Ottawa a two-goal lead en route to a 2-1 win. "I think what I'm most proud of with him, honestly, it's not that he played his first NHL game or that he scored, that's awesome stuff, but it's the story behind it and the resilience and perseverance and fight that he showed," Brian Boucher said. "He really dug in. I mean, he's had nothing but setbacks and disappointments for five years since being drafted. I'm sure he questioned, and I know I did deep down inside, would this day ever come. To play in the NHL, it's a privilege, it's not a right, and I'm so happy he was able to fulfill his dream of getting that game and scoring. items.title: Former NHLer Craig Anderson says his game slipped following release of GTA 5
items.summary: GTA 6, the next installment in the popular video game franchise, is set to be released on Thursday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-USA TODAY Sports Grand Theft Auto IV (GTA 6), the long-awaited next installment in the ultra-popular video game franchise, is finally set to be released on Thursday. While you wouldn’t think the release of a new video game would have any effect on an NHL season, former NHL goaltender Craig Anderson is here to tell you otherwise. On Wednesday’s episode of the Absolute Non-Sens podcast, Anderson revealed that the release of GTA 5 directly led to a drop-off in his play back in 2013 while with the Ottawa Senators . “My worst season that I felt I had in Ottawa, was the year that ‘Grand Theft Auto V’ came out,” Anderson said. “Direct correlation. Just a time suck. You’d play after a game, you’d get home 11-11:30, you’d start playing that game and it’d be 4 AM and you’d be like ‘I’m not even tired’. Now Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out so it’ll be interesting to see how that all plays out.” While the 2013-14 season wasn’t actually Anderson’s worst with the Senators, as his play tailed off pretty dramatically in his age-36 season of 2017-18, his numbers that year do stand out as noticeably worse than those from the seasons surrounding it, lending credence to his GTA 5 theory. In the 2012-13 season, the Park Ridge, Illinois native led the league with a .941 save percentage and a 1.68 goals-against average, finishing fourth in voting for the Vezina Trophy. In 2013-14, he dipped to a .911 SV% and a 3.00 GAA, before bouncing back to a .923 SV% and a 2.49 GAA in 2014-15. He then followed that up by scoring twice on the power play, 36 seconds apart, to complete his second career hat trick. His hat-trick goal would serve as the game-winner after Jake DeBrusk scored late in a comeback attempt for Vancouver. items.summary: It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud.
items.body: CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Pa. — It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud. Asked Wednesday what gives him hope that his struggling team, which is mired near the bottom of the Eastern Conference and has three regulation wins through 20 games, can turn it around in time to salvage this season, Dubas turned philosophical. Yes, making the playoffs for a second straight year would be nice. Yet that's not the metric he will lean on to gauge progress. Dubas would like the team's younger players to take “major steps.” He'd like to see the iconic, aging core led by captain Sidney Crosby show it still has “gas left in the tank." He'd like some of the prospects he's acquired since taking over to make a push for NHL playing time. If those things can happen, Dubas believes the franchise will be on “the right track" regardless of where the Penguins wind up in the standings. Then, Dubas finished by using a phrase that included the one word he has consistently avoided uttering publicly since taking over in the summer of 2023. “This has been, I think rightfully, an unorthodox style of rebuilding a team because of the players that are here,” he said. items.summary: The Oilers are becoming a different team under Mike Babcock. They’re finding ways to win beyond McDavid and Draisaitl, playing a more complete brand of hockey, and closing the gap on the NHL’s elite.
items.body: We’ve written a lot over the years about an Oilers team that needed to get “one win better” after the 2024 Final, or find “just a few more periods of winning hockey” after losing to Florida again in 2025. Of course, it doesn’t work quite that way. When you win six playoff series in two years, you’re obviously doing most things right. The Leafs have won just eight playoff rounds this century, Vancouver nine, Montreal 13, and Calgary five. Edmonton has been elite, but still, Florida had something that they did not. You can’t change out your entire roster, but you can change how your roster plays. That’s what Mike Babcock is in the process of doing these days. The same players, mostly, are playing a different brand of hockey. And if there is one surprise in Edmonton, it’s that almost all of them are succeeding at the transition. items.body: Pittsburgh Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas doesn't seem eager to give up valuable assets in order to improve his team's position in the Metropolitan Division. Speaking during his quarter-mark-of-the-season news conference , Dubas acknowledged that he has seen flashes of the team he wants Pittsburgh to become, but the consistency hasn't been there. The Penguins sit seventh in the Metropolitan Division and the organization is in a position where it has to decide whether to make additions to a veteran roster or continue prioritizing its long-term plans. Dubas didn't hesitate to make his position clear on moving out future assets this season to remain competitive. “No, we wouldn’t,” Dubas said. “I don't think it's prudent for the Pittsburgh Penguins to give up future draft picks or prospects to add more veterans to our group.” While Dubas isn't ruling out making trades, the Penguins are more likely to explore opportunities involving younger players who could benefit from a change of scenery. One example Dubas pointed to from last season was trading for Egor Chinakhov. The National Hockey League unveiled the uniforms each team will wear for the upcoming Winter Classic on Wednesday. The outdoor game will take place at Rice-Eccles Stadium on the University of Utah campus in Salt Lake City on New Year's Eve. It marks Utah's first outdoor game and the first played by the Mammoth, the lone franchise that hasn't played one yet. It also marks the 47th regular-season outdoor game all-time. The uniforms are designed by Fanatics, the NHL's official outfitter, and are heavily inspired by the ski culture shared by Utah and Colorado. The Mammoth are set to wear a light-blue jersey with brown and beige detailing, featuring a woolly mammoth on the crest. Meanwhile, the Avalanche uniforms are burgundy, navy and beige, drawing on jersey designs from the franchise's past, with the front crest featuring a 'C' with mountains inside. The NHL Winter Classic will be aired on Sportsnet on Thursday, Dec. 31 (6 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. MT).

items.title: Boston College to retire Johnny Gaudreau’s No. 13
items.summary: The late Johnny Gaudreau had 175 points in his collegiate career with Boston College and won the Hobey Baker Award in 2014.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Johnny Gaudreau at Boston College The Boston College Eagles men’s hockey program announced on Wednesday that it will retire the iconic No. 13 jersey once worn by the late Johnny Gaudreau on Feb. 12, 2027. Gaudreau, who spent the 2011-12 through 2013-14 seasons in Chestnut Hill before beginning his NHL career, is one of the most decorated players in the storied program’s history. He produced 175 points in 119 career games, helped lead the program to the national championship in 2012, and won the Hobey Baker Memorial Award as collegiate hockey’s top player in 2014. “We are proud to honor Johnny Gaudreau by retiring his No. 13 at Boston College,” Boston College athletic director Blake James said via the school’s press release. “Johnny was an extraordinary player who helped bring a national championship to the Heights and became one of the most accomplished players in our program’s history. He will always hold a special place in the Boston College family.” Gaudreau, along with his younger brother and fellow Boston College alum Matthew, passed away in August of 2024 when they were struck and killed by a motor vehicle while riding bikes near their hometown of Carneys Point, New Jersey. items.body: Designs for Avalanche, Mammoth inspired by outdoor hockey, alpine nostalgia NEW YORK – Today, the National Hockey League (NHL) and Fanatics, the authentic outfitter of the NHL, unveiled uniforms for the Discover NHL Winter Classic, to be worn when the Utah Mammoth host the Colorado Avalanche on New Year’s Eve at Rice-Eccles Stadium on the campus of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City. items.summary: Jonathan Castagna stole the show on Tuesday with his first two NHL goals, which were key to the Flames’ second win in three California road games.
items.body: On any other night, stripping Macklin Celebrini from a pretty good scoring opportunity would have been a highlight for Jonathan Castagna . But it paled in comparison to the fact he finished the night with the first two goals of his NHL career. “I’m really grateful for the opportunity in the first place,” the rookie centre told Sportsnet’s Brendan Parker following the Flames’ 5-2 win in San Jose. “To score a goal in this league is a really special moment. It’s been a long time coming. There have been a lot of chances I wish I could have back.” Castagna, who was acquired last season in the MacKenzie Weegar deal, was called up early from the Wranglers this season and has made it clear with his 200-foot game he isn’t going back. He extended the Flames lead to 4-1 early in the third when he fought his way to the front of the net and turned to bat in an Aydar Suniev rebound out of the air to kickstart a celebration that saw his teammates shower him with water as he did his fly-by. “They were spraying me with water pretty good — I was trying not to smile, and keep it cool, but it was a pretty special moment and I was smiling ear-to-ear,” said the Toronto native. “It’s really nice to finally get one in the back of the net, but also see the reaction from the guys being like that — it’s heartwarming.” With the net empty, and things getting chippy, Castagna batted in another one after Martin Pospisil did his best to ensure he got the puck to the popular young centre who swept it in. On a night when Pospisil and Matt Coronato scored to put the Flames up 2-1 in the first period, it was Castagna and another Flame who stole the show with milestone moments that were key to the team’s second win in three California road games. items.title: Gauthier ‘just flowing’ during 10-game goal streak for Ducks
items.summary: ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines.
items.body: Forward closing in on Selanne after fourth hat trick of season in loss to Blues ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines. So, the Anaheim Ducks forward is doing his best to adopt tunnel vision as he continues to score goals at a record pace. That was evident again on Tuesday, when he extended his goal streak to 10 games by getting a hat trick, his fourth during the run, in an 8-6 loss to the St. Louis Blues at Enterprise Center. ANA@STL: Gauthier records his fourth hat trick of the season and fifth of his career The 22-year-old, who also had an assist in the loss, has 19 goals during the streak, which is one game shy of tying Teemu Selanne (Oct. 21 to Nov. 10, 1997) for the longest in Ducks history. He's also the third player in NHL history to have a goal streak of at least 10 games before the age of 23, joining Babe Dye (11 games in 1920-21) and Mike Bossy (10 games in 1978-79). "It obviously gets published a lot what’s going on, but if I let the online chats and stuff, the pressure and all that stuff, get to me, it’s not going to be good," Gauthier told NHL.com. "When I play at my best, I’m playing free. I’m not thinking, I’m just flowing, I’m using my instincts and being great. I don’t let that affect me. I haven’t these last handful of weeks, so I’m going to keep that going." Gauthier certainly hasn't let it affect him, considering he has 24 points (19 goals, five assists) during an NHL career-high 12-game point streak. He also has 21 goals in 21 games this season, which is tied with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers for the NHL lead. The Leafs found fresh ways to stunt their momentum, allowing Chicago to strike back 35 seconds and 12 seconds, respectively, after their second- and third-period comeback goals. And the head man inside those visitors' coaching quarters boarded a plane home more disappointed than usual. “I’m disappointed tonight,” Jim Hiller said. “I’m disappointed every night. "I view it as part of my game I want to play, and I take that as my job that game, and it contributes to the team," Hischier said. "I obviously take pride in that. items.title: Oilers’ lineup shuffle pays off in decisive win over Panthers
items.summary: After splitting Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl up on Tuesday, the Oilers proceeded to put the boots to the Panthers for their sixth straight win.
items.body: It was inevitable that head coach Mike Babcock would have to split up his best two players, charging Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl with the assignment of running their own lines, after playing 22 straight games together this season. What you’re never sure of, however, is how long it might take for a team to adapt to change, after playing a quarter of a season with a certain deployment. “Coming into the game, we knew that without Nuge we probably weren't deep enough to go the way we've been going,” said Babcock, who was without second-line centre Ryan Nugent-Hopkins (illness) for a second straight game. “But we got a real good game out of (Owen) Michaels' line, a good game from Dickey's (Jason Dickinson’s third) line. Our top two lines were good… Edmonton walked into a building in Sunrise, Fla., where it had lost two Stanley Cup Finals, and put the boots to the Florida Panthers 5-2. The Oilers led 2-0 after one period, 4-0 after two, and after a pair of Matthew Tkachuk goals in garbage time, Leon Draisaitl potted his league-leading 21st into an empty net to cap a decisive 5-2 win. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matthew Schaefer can’t stop making history. The New York Islanders’ defenseman scored a hat trick during the team’s 5-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets Tuesday night, becoming the third teenage defenseman in NHL history to record three goals in a game. The other two teenage defenders to achieve the feat were Phil Housley and Hannu Virta, both with the Buffalo Sabres during the 1982-83 season. Schaefer, 19, finished the night with three goals and nine shots in 23:23 of ice time. The Islanders are now 10-6-4 with 24 points this season. Through 20 games in 2026-27, Schaefer has nine goals and 15 assists for 24 points, averaging 26:58 of ice time per game. The Hamilton, Ont., native has 32 goals and 51 assists for 83 points in 102 career NHL contests. Schaefer is coming off one of the most impressive seasons for a rookie defenseman in NHL history. He finished with 23 goals and 36 assists for 59 points, averaged 24:41 of ice time per game, capped off by winning the 2026 Calder Trophy for rookie of the year . His 23 goals placed him second among all NHL defenseman in 2025-26, behind only Jakob Chychrun of the Washington Capitals . He made NHL history by tying Hockey Hall of Famer Brian Leetch for the most goals by a rookie defender , and also became the youngest blueliner in NHL history to reach 50 points in a season . Schaefer was selected by the Islanders with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NHL Entry Draft, despite the fact he played just 73 career OHL regular-season games due to injuries. items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist to extend his season-opening points streak to 23 games, and the Edmonton Oilers continued their sizzling start by beating the rival Florida Panthers 5-2 on Tuesday night. McDavid now has 13 goals and 42 assists, and the 23-game streak to start a season ties Wayne Gretzky for the fifth-longest in NHL history. Only Gretzky (51- and 30-game streaks), Quebec's Mats Sundin (30) and Pittsburgh's Mario Lemieux (28) had longer streaks to open a season. Vasily Podkolzin scored twice, while Kasperi Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl each had a goal and two assists for Edmonton, which lost the 2024 and 2025 Stanley Cup finals to Florida. Devon Levi got the win in net for the Oilers, improving to 10-1-0 on the season. Matthew Tkachuk scored twice in the third period for Florida, which trailed 4-0 entering the final minutes. It was his first multi-goal game of the season. Edmonton (17-3-3) won its sixth straight and has 37 points through 23 games, tying for the second-most in team history. The 55 points through 23 games have McDavid in elite company. Only two other players — Gretzky and Lemieux, both doing it on three occasions — have managed that many points this quickly into a season. Lemieux was the last to do it, posting 66 points through 23 games in 1995-96. The Panthers were again without forwards Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, who have both been sidelined for all but two games of the season. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said both are expected to meet with physicians later this week, an indicator that their returns to the lineup could be looming.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined Ottawa’s Fabian Zetterlund’s presence and contact in the crease impaired Stuart Skinner’s ability to play his position prior to Dylan Cozen’s goal. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 69.1 which states, in part, “Goals should be disallowed only if: (1) an attacking player, either by his positioning or by contact, impairs the goalkeeper’s ability to move freely within his crease or defend his goal.”

items.body: Olczyk, Savard, Roenick, Chelios and Foley discuss historic 100-year anniversary for franchise CHICAGO – It’s been 100 years for the Chicago Blackhawks, and they wrapped up their Centennial celebration prior to their game against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday. Along with a one-night-only exhibit featuring rare artifacts, historic memorabilia and photography in the atrium section of United Center, the Blackhawks had all five of their ambassadors take part in a Q&A about 90 minutes before the game: former forwards Eddie Olczyk , Denis Savard and Jeremy Roenick , former defenseman Chris Chelios and former play-by-play broadcaster Pat Foley. Tuesday marked the 100th anniversary of the first game in Blackhawks history, a 4-1 win against the Toronto St. Patricks on Nov. 17, 1926. “Pat, what was the traffic like getting to that first game?” Olczyk said to Foley. Olczyk was Foley’s broadcast partner with the Blackhawks from 2006-22. The five talked for about 20 minutes about the history of the Blackhawks, including the old Chicago Stadium, where the team played from 1929-94. all smiles when you get this squad together 😂❤️ pic.twitter.com/BpLn2ztJGs “(Nothing like it), especially growing up here in Chicago as a fan and being in the crowd,” said Chelios, who was traded from the Montreal Canadiens to his hometown Blackhawks for Savard on June 29, 1990. “That’s really the only reason why I knew what to expect when I got traded here.” “To walk up those stairs, hear the crowd that brought out sometimes the best, sometimes the worst, but anybody playing against us knew they were up for war. It was the toughest place to play for the opposition. The fans were great; it was smoke filled in the rafters. Those old buildings, but especially old Chicago stadium, I loved playing there.”

Leading the comeback with a four-point effort and the shootout winner over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday, Scheifele passed his mentor Dale Hawerchuk for most career points in franchise history with 933. The milestone carried some added weight, as the history-making coincided with the Jets' mentors trip. Shifting from the traditional "dad's trip," every player got to invite a male mentor on Winnipeg's two-game road swing through Dallas and Chicago. Scheifele, whose father, Brad, died of cancer in May 2025, invited Gregg Derlago, his billet dad during his early years in Winnipeg. Derlago had given Scheifele a pin with a picture of him and his dad when he was younger, which he wore after the game while being interviewed by reporters. "He's up there watching, and Dale's up there watching as well," Scheifele said. "Pretty special to do this tonight with all the mentors here. items.title: Mantha, Kovacevic out at least one month for Devils
items.summary: Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic will be out for an extended period, New Jersey Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said on Tuesday.
items.body: Forward sustained fractured throat, defenseman has high ankle sprain Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic will be out for an extended period, New Jersey Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said on Tuesday. Mantha is projected to be out one month after the forward had surgery Monday to repair a fracture in his throat. He was injured in a 5-4 overtime win at the New York Islanders on Nov. 7 but should be able to resume skating in the near future. However, it’s uncertain when Mantha will be able to return. The Devils will need to evaluate when Mantha can safely withstand contact because of the unusual nature of the injury. "That one, I guess, from the way it's described to me, is going to be a tricky one because it's a very rare injury for any athlete, really," Keefe said. "So, it's just more so about when he'll be ready to take contact again, and they're going to feel that out." Kovacevic, a defenseman, is expected to miss 4-6 weeks because of a high ankle sprain he sustained in a 5-2 loss at the Winnipeg Jets on Nov. 10. He has two assists in 13 games and averages 14:40 of ice time. Brett Pesce (illness), however, was a full participant at practice Tuesday and is expected to return against the Montreal Canadiens at Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey, on Wednesday (7:30 p.m. ET; MSGSN, Prime). The defenseman missed two games. Seamus Casey took another step in his recovery by skating on his own Tuesday. However, Keefe said he had not received an updated timetable for when the defenseman can play. Casey had knee surgery at the beginning of October after being injured during a preseason game at the New York Rangers on Sept. 24. The initial timeline for his recovery was 8-10 weeks.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: (Steven Ellis/The Nation Network) The St. Louis Blues announced Tuesday that forward Adam Jecho has been cleared through the NHL/NHLPA Player Assistance Program and will rejoin the organization. The team said Jecho has been assigned to the Springfield Thunderbirds, their American Hockey League affiliate, and will report immediately. The league announced in September that Jecho would receive care from the player assistance program. A native of Zlin, Czechia, Jecho was taken No. 95 overall in the third round of the 2024 NHL Entry Draft. He signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the Blues that kicked in this season and will last through the 2028-29 campaign. The 6-foot-5 center spent three seasons with the Western Hockey League’s Edmonton Oil Kings, where he scored 58 goals and added 78 assists for 136 points in 157 career regular-season games. His best season came in 2024-25 where he recorded 25 goals and 28 assists for 53 points in 56 games. Going into Tuesday, the Blues are 9-9-2 with 20 points through their first 20 games of the 2026-27 regular season. They are seventh in the Central Division and three points back of the second Wildcard spot in the Western Conference. The Blues have a three-way tie for the team lead in points , with forwards Jimmy Snuggerud, Dylan Holloway and Robert Thomas all having 14 points. Snuggerud, 22, leads the team with 10 goals while Thomas leads with 11 assists. Philip Broberg leads all defenders with four goals and nine assists for 13 points and is averaging a team-high 24:33 of ice time per game.

Myers’ injury only adds to the injuries suffered by the Stars’ blueliners this season. items.title: Sharks’ Kiefer Sherwood out week-to-week with upper-body injury
items.summary: Kiefer Sherwood has two goals and eight points in 23 games with the San Jose Sharks in 2026-27.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Gonzales The San Jose Sharks will be without one of their veteran forwards for the foreseeable future. Head coach Ryan Warsofsky told reporters Tuesday that Kiefer Sherwood will be out week-to-week with an upper-body injury, but that he doesn’t require surgery. Sherwood appeared to suffer the injury during the Sharks’ 4-2 win over the Nashville Predators Sunday. He finished the game with two shots and two hits in 10:55 of ice time. Sherwood, 31, has two goals and six assists for eight points in 23 games with the Sharks in 2026-27. He is in the first year of a five-year contract extension that carries a cap hit of $5.75 million through the 2030-31 season . Now in his ninth NHL season, the Columbus native has 68 goals and 74 assists for 142 points in 360 career regular-season games with the Sharks, Predators, Vancouver Canucks , Colorado Avalanche and Anaheim Ducks . His best offensive season came with the Canucks in 2024-25 where he scored 19 goals and added 21 assists for 40 points. Sherwood also has a goal and assist in eight playoff contests. The Sharks are 10-11-2 with 22 points through 23 games in 2026-27. They are fourth in the Pacific Division and one point back of the second Wildcard spot in the Western Conference. Captain Macklin Celebrini leads the team in all offensive categories with nine goals and 18 assists for 27 points. He also leads the team in ice time, averaging 23:07 per night. Meanwhile, defenseman Jacob Trouba is averaging 22:15 of ice time per game. Rookie forward Ivar Stenberg, the 2026 No. 2 overall pick, has seven goals and seven assists for 14 points in 23 games.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: George Walker IV-USA TODAY Sports An underrated netminder is officially making the move to North America. On Tuesday, the Vegas Vanguards announced that the team has signed goaltender Saskia Maurer to a two-year contract, which will carry through the 2027-28 season. Maurer was taken by the Vanguards in the fourth round, 41st overall, of the 2026 PWHL Draft . She was the team’s fifth selection in the draft, and the fourth goaltender taken in Detroit . The Swiss netminder admitted she’s excited about the opportunity to play in the fast-growing league. “I’m really excited to join Las Vegas and be part of this team,” Maurer said in a release. “It’s a great new challenge, and I’m looking forward to getting started and seeing where this journey takes us.” Maurer has made a name for herself on the international stage. She has been part of Switzerland’s senior national team since the 2019 IIHF Women’s World Championship, backing up Andrea Brandli for the past few years. She also represented her country at the Winter Olympics in 2022 and 2026, really helping Switzerland play well in the group stage with Brandli missing the first couple of games due to Norovirus this past February. In Milan, Maurer went 1-2-0, with a 3.25 goals-against average and a .918 save percentage, helping Switzerland win its first Olympic bronze medal in 12 years. Maurer held a similar role during the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. With a 1-2-0 record again, she also had a 1.67 GAA and a .944 SV%. Sokolowski-USA TODAY Sports It looks like some people are trying to take action against the International Ice Hockey Federation for their recent decisions. On Tuesday, the IIHF website was the victim of a cyberattack. items.title: Flames’ Huberdeau seeks more answers as he returns to action
items.summary: The toughest part of Jonathan Huberdeau’s hip resurfacing recovery wasn’t the pain, the gruelling rehabilitation or even the first three months he spent unable to skate. It was the uncertainty.
items.body: CALGARY — The toughest part of Jonathan Huberdeau ’s hip resurfacing recovery wasn’t the pain, the gruelling rehabilitation or even the first three months he spent unable to skate. Would he play again? Would the pain return? Would he ever be the same player? And, perhaps most importantly, would he be able to enjoy a normal life without constantly wondering what his hip had in store for him? “I think it's just ups and downs,” Huberdeau said, describing the mental gymnastics of an eight-month rehabilitation following surgery. “Are you gonna come back, or are you gonna be as good as before? Better than before? Not as good? There was some point that I was hurting a lot, and you're like, ‘OK, well, is it gonna be like this for the rest of my life?” Devin Cooley, the Flames' resident philosopher, certainly has a gift for putting things in perspective. Whatever the secret, Huberdeau is finally ready to put the uncertainty behind him and get back to playing hockey. The 33-year-old Flames winger will make his long-awaited return to game action Wednesday night at the Saddledome when he suits up for the Calgary Wranglers on an injury conditioning loan that represents the biggest milestone yet in his comeback from surgery last March. Eight months after going under the knife, he's nervous, excited and understandably eager to find out what happens when the puck drops. “I mean, I haven't played for a while. I think that's just a normal part. But I just gotta take it and embrace it.” The date has been a moving target since he shut things down last February, with Huberdeau wisely resisting the temptation to put a firm timetable on a procedure so uncommon among hockey players that there isn't much of a playbook. That Nov. 3 win has galvanized the Jets, who have won six in a row, including erasing another four-goal deficit Saturday against the Chicago Blackhawks. (Winnipeg became the second team in NHL history with multiple four-goal comeback wins over a six-game span.) “To see the character in this room that there’s no giving up, there’s always fight and especially at a time when we lost a bunch in a row and it’s really easy to lay your gloves down and be done and move on to the next one, to see the team keep fighting and get that win (against the Canadiens), it’s almost impossible not to get a spark out of that,” Jets centre and new franchise points leader Mark Scheifele told reporters . items.title: Flames loan Jonathan Huberdeau to AHL for conditioning stint
items.summary: The 33-year-old is likely to make his return on Tuesday against the Coachella Valley Firebirds.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Calgary Flames forward Jonathan Huberdeau is making his way back to competitive hockey, but will begin his comeback with a conditioning stint with the AHL’s Calgary Wranglers, who share the Scotiabank Saddledome with the NHL club. Under the terms of the CBA, a player who has been out with a long-term injury, defined as missing at least 24 days and 10 games, can be sent to the AHL on a conditioning loan. The loan is limited to three games or six games, whichever is longer, but can be extended by two additional games at request. While he is with the Wranglers, Huberdeau won’t count towards Calgary’s active NHL roster, but will count towards the NHL salary cap. The 33-year-old Huberdeau underwent hip surgery in the spring and has not played a competitive game since Feb. 4, when he scored in a 4-3 Flames win over the Edmonton Oilers . Before his injury, he posted 10 goals and 15 assists in 50 games with the Flames, bringing his NHL career totals to 263 goals, 544 assists and 807 points in 962 games since making his debut with the Florida Panthers in the 2012-13 season. “I’m feeling pretty good. It’s a big surgery,” Huberdeau said in September. “There’s no pain anymore, which is nice to deal with. Just now, the goal is to come back and be 100%.” Now with the Wranglers, he could return at home on Tuesday and Wednesday night against the Coachella Valley Firebirds, before the team heads on the road to take on the Laval Rocket on Saturday and Sunday. If his recovery and form-building remain on track, he could be with the Flames as soon as next week, as they enjoy a mediocre start to the 2026-27 season, with 19 points in their first 21 games and four short of the final Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.
